facts.text: AAA's third-party on-road tests found nighttime performance cliffs that standard daytime protocols did not reveal.

facts.text: In AAA's October 2019 on-road tests, none of four vehicles avoided a pedestrian target at night at 25 mph.

facts.text: In a study published 16 October 2025, AAA and the Automobile Club of Southern California Automotive Research Center tested a 2024 Honda Accord, 2025 Toyota Camry, 2025 Chevrolet Malibu and 2025 Tesla Model 3 at 25 mph (40 km/h).

facts.text: AAA's on-road study published 16 October 2025 reported that nighttime pedestrian automatic emergency braking (PAEB) impact avoidance improved from 0% in 2019 to 60% in 2025, leaving roughly 40% failures under ideal conditions.
facts.quote: "Nighttime PAEB impact avoidance improved from 0% in 2019 to 60% in 2025", that is roughly 40% failures under "ideal conditions"

facts.text: The 2025 Toyota Camry avoided impact in all its nighttime runs in AAA's on-road PAEB study published 16 October 2025.
facts.quote: the Camry avoided impact in all its night runs

facts.text: The 2025 Chevrolet Malibu scored lowest among the four vehicles in AAA's on-road PAEB study published 16 October 2025.
High-visibility clothing caused a complete loss of detection in some systems in AAA's on-road PAEB tests reported in the study published 16 October 2025.
facts.quote: High-visibility clothing caused a complete loss of detection in some systems.

facts.text: The nighttime and high-visibility-clothing conditions highlighted by AAA's on-road PAEB tests were under-represented in consumer test protocols.

facts.text: AAA's on-road PAEB test case shows that protocol-based evidence, whether physical or virtual, gives false confidence outside the protocol's envelope.
